question: When do we consider that two medications are bioequivalent ?:

options.opa: The pharmacological effect of both is identical.
options.opb: The pharmacological effect and the bioavailability are the same.
options.opc: The speed of disposition (Cmax and Tmax) and the bioavailability of the active principle are practically the same.
options.opd: The speed of disposition (Cmax and Tmax) and the clearance of the active principle are practically the same.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Bioequivalence" -> "similar pharmacokinetic profile" -> "similar Cmax and Tmax" -> "similar bioavailability" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Bioequivalence" -> "similar speed of disposition" -> "similar Cmax" -> "similar Tmax" -> "similar bioavailability" -> 85%
analysis: Bioequivalence between two medications is determined when they have similar bioavailability and similar pharmacokinetic properties, specifically the rate and extent of absorption. This is typically assessed by comparing the maximum concentration (Cmax) and the time to reach maximum concentration (Tmax) of the active ingredient in the bloodstream. Therefore, the correct option is the one that mentions both the speed of disposition (Cmax and Tmax) and bioavailability.
